Done. `/app/answers.json` is written and valid, with the full budget used (10 runs, 1.98e19 of 2e19 FLOPs).

**What I found**

- **The notebook's fit was contaminated.** It treated intermediate cosine checkpoints as finished runs. Every checkpoint carries an extra "un-annealed" penalty, so the notes overstated how fast loss falls with data and pushed the compute-optimal size too small.
- **Clean structure in the simulator.** Finished-run loss follows an additive law in N and D with exponents about 0.38 and 0.34. On top of it, every checkpoint sits above the finished-run law by a penalty that depends only on the current learning rate, not on N, D or fraction. WSD checkpoints in the stable phase are all exactly ~0.296 nats high. Cosine checkpoints decay toward ~0.03 at the end, which is why finished cosine trails finished WSD by that amount.
- **Fit quality.** Residual RMS across 272 points is 0.0045 nats, at the seed-noise level (~0.01 at N=2e7). Per-size fits give the same data exponent at every N, so extrapolation to 3e9 parameters is on solid ground.

**Answers**

| id | answer | basis |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | B (N=2.4e9) | lowest predicted loss at 1.08e21 FLOPs in every fit variant, margin ~0.02 nats over A and C |
| q2 | 2.69 | WSD law at N=3e9, D=6e10 (range across fit variants 2.67 to 2.70) |
| q3 | 0.193 | cosine penalty at 40%, measured directly and scale-independent |
| q4 | 0.0225 to 0.253 | gap at f_stop=0.9 (lo) and 0.5 (hi), data term plus penalty difference |
| q5 | supported | the 70% checkpoint is ~0.04 nats below a finished WSD run on 40% of the tokens, in every fit |

**Caveat.** q5 rests on a ~0.04 nat margin, roughly four times the seed noise. It hinges on the data exponent holding out to 6e10 tokens, which the per-size fits support but the lab cannot test beyond 1.1e10.
